title: Pick the standard interface that fits each job

blocks.text: `java.util.function` has one interface for each shape of job. A `Consumer<T>` takes a value and returns nothing, a `Supplier<T>` takes nothing and returns a value, a `Function<T, R>` turns one value into another, a `Predicate<T>` answers yes or no, and a `BinaryOperator<T>` combines two values of one type. Writing `Function<String, Void>` and returning `null` is the sign that a `Consumer` was wanted.
Write the static factories of `Handlers`, each returning the interface named in its signature:

rows: adds every accepted string to `sink`, repeats included

blocks.text: A factory's supplier is called many times over its life, and "first, then second" is a promise about order.

cases.says: Each factory works over its whole input range: every string is appended, repeats too; only a capital A counts, and the empty string is no match; larger never overflows.
A Supplier used as a factory hands out a new list on every get, never the same one twice.
Consumer.andThen runs the receiver first and the argument second.

origin.section: Common Pitfalls and How to Avoid Them

concepts: Consumer.andThen runs two consumers one after the other, the receiver first.
Consumer takes and returns nothing, Supplier gives without taking, Function transforms, Predicate tests, and BinaryOperator combines two of one type.
